{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Identify and keep only the latest sample_seq per patient
# This ensures we only use the most recent measurement for each patient
trial_df = trial_df.sort_values('sample_seq', ascending=False)
trial_df = trial_df.drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Verify the result: should now have one row per patient
print(f"Number of unique patients: {trial_df['patient_id'].nunique()}")
print(f"Number of rows after deduplication: {len(trial_df)}")

# Check the distribution of arms and severity
print("\nArm distribution:")
print(trial_df['arm'].value_counts())

print("\nSeverity distribution by arm:")
print(pd.crosstab(trial_df['arm'], trial_df['severity']))

# Check for sentinel values in biomarker_baseline and biomarker_final
print("\nSentinel values in biomarker_baseline:")
print(trial_df['biomarker_baseline'].unique())

print("\nSentinel values in biomarker_final:")
print(trial_df['biomarker_final'].unique())

# Check if biomarker_final is missing or invalid
print("\nMissing biomarker_final:")
print(trial_df['biomarker_final'].isna().sum())"}
